open_obligations: Note fixed rounds versus judge-ended sessions.
Check whether Khan et al. run consultancy for both correct and incorrect assignments, and if so whether that changes how accuracy should be aggregated compared with 50% random assignment.
Check argument length matching between debate and consultancy.
out.other_title: Consultancy baseline: single expert argues for an answer that is correct 50% of the time
out.rationale: Michael et al. define consultancy with a single expert assigned the correct or incorrect answer with 50% probability and judge-ended sessions. Khan et al. use the consultancy baseline established by Michael et al. for comparison with debate, with an LLM consultant for a pre-determined number of rounds matching debate.
out.scope: proposed DEPENDS_ON: single-expert consultancy as a non-adversarial baseline for debate, adapted to LLM consultants with fixed rounds

text: Following Michael et al. (2023), the authors use consultancy as a baseline in which a single expert model (the consultant) is assigned a specific answer and tries to persuade the judge it is correct, while the judge asks probing questions to elicit the correct answer; consultancy runs for the same pre-determined number of rounds as debate.
title: Consultancy baseline: single expert model argues for an assigned answer
